mapei/mapesil-ac.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies depending on the joint size. The printed expansion joint table runs from 25 ml per linear metre at 5 x 5 mm to 1000 ml at 50 x 20 mm, with a 310 ml cartridge yielding 3.1 m at 10 x 10 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-ac.caveat: Width times depth in millimetres is the millilitres per linear metre exactly, with no constant. All 10 printed expansion joint rows, all 7 printed fillet rows and all 10 printed 310 ml cartridge yields reproduce, 27 of 27 cells. The depth is the sheet's own: equal to the width up to 10 mm, 10 mm for widths of 10 to 20 mm, then half the width capped at 20 mm. Cartridges come in boxes of 12. On absorbent substrates the sheet also calls for Mapei Primerseal A or M at 100 to 300 g/m2, at a primer volume of no more than 5 percent of the sealant volume.

mapei/mapesil-lm.source: JOINT SIZING AND CONSUMPTION: metres of product per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm and 0.4 m at 40 x 20 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-lm.caveat: The printed yields are 310 ml divided by the joint section: all 8 butt rows reproduce, and 3 of the 4 fillet rows. The 15 mm fillet row prints 3 m where the section gives 2.8 m, so that one row of the sheet is about 8 percent optimistic. Cartridges come in self supporting boxes of 12.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-45-ft.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-45-ft.caveat: Also supplied in 600 ml cartridges, boxes of 20, where the same table prints 24, 6, 4, 3, 1.9 and 1.3 m. All 6 printed rows of the 300 ml column and all 6 of the 600 ml column reproduce as the pack size divided by the joint section, rounded down. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-ms-45.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ms-45.caveat: Also supplied in 600 ml sausages, boxes of 20. All 6 printed rows of the 300 ml table reproduce as 300 divided by the joint section, rounded down. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-ms-crystal.source: CONSUMPTION TABLE: linear metres per cartridge, 12 m at 5 x 5 mm, 3 m at 10 x 10 mm, 2 m at 15 x 10 mm, 1.5 m at 20 x 10 mm, 0.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 0.6 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ms-crystal.caveat: All 6 printed rows reproduce as 300 divided by the joint section, rounded down. Supplied in boxes of 12 cartridges. Used as an adhesive instead of a sealant, the sheet gives no rate at all: it depends on whether the product is applied in beads or spots.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-s25.source: CONSUMPTION FOR 600 ML CARTRIDGE: 24 m at 5 x 5 mm, 6 m at 10 x 10 mm, 5.3 m at 15 x 7.5 mm, 3 m at 20 x 10 mm, 1.9 m at 25 x 12.5 mm and 1.3 m at 30 x 15 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-s25.caveat: All 6 printed rows reproduce as 600 divided by the joint section. Note the sheet pairs 15 mm wide with only 7.5 mm deep, not the 10 mm its sister products use. Supplied in boxes of 24 sausages.

mapei/mapesil-z-plus.source: COVERAGE TABLE (linear metres per cartridge): butt joint 11 m at 5 x 5 mm, 2.8 m at 10 x 10 mm, 1.4 m at 20 x 10 mm and 0.4 m at 40 x 20 mm.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapesil-z-plus.caveat: All 7 printed butt rows and all 4 printed triangular rows reproduce as 280 divided by the joint section, 11 of 11 cells. The cartridge is 280 ml here, not the 310 ml of the rest of the Mapesil range, and comes in boxes of 12.

mapei/mapeflex-psu-sl-me.source: CONSUMPTION: litres per linear metre, 0.050 for a 10 x 5 mm joint, 0.200 for 20 x 10 mm, 0.800 for 40 x 20 mm and 1.250 for 50 x 25 mm.

pack.label: pack of A plus B (5 litres)

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-psu-sl-me.caveat: All 4 printed cells reproduce exactly: a litre per metre is 1000 ml of joint section, so 20 x 10 mm is 0.200 litres. The sheet allows joints from 5 to 50 mm wide, asks for a 2 to 1 width to depth ratio, and sets minimum depths of 5 mm on metals, glass and other non porous surfaces, 10 mm on all porous surfaces and 20 mm on trafficked joints and joints under hydrostatic pressure. The pouring grade SL ME comes in 5 litre A plus B packs; the gun grade NS ME in 4 litre packs; density is 1.55 to 1.66 kg per litre.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-70-sl.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption of sealant in kg per metre, 0.04 at 5 x 5 mm, 0.15 at 10 x 10 mm, 0.29 at 20 x 10 mm, 0.65 at 30 x 15 mm and 1.16 at 40 x 20 mm, with a density of 1.45 g per cm3.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-pu-70-sl.caveat: The calculator gives the joint volume in millilitres. The sheet's own kilogrammes are that volume times its printed density of 1.45 g per cm3, and all 8 printed kg per metre cells reproduce that way. It is sold in 10 kg kits of A plus B, for which the sheet prints 276, 69, 46, 34, 22, 15, 11 and 9 metres across those eight joint sizes, so divide the litres by 6.9 for kits. Primer PU60 is a separate line at a tenth of the sealant, 0.013 kg per metre at 10 x 10 mm. The printed rates are theoretical and carry no waste.

mapei/mapeflex-ac4.source: RATIO WIDTH / DEPTH OF THE JOINT: up to 10 mm wide the depth is the same as the width, from 11 to 20 mm the depth is 10 mm in all cases, and above 20 mm the depth is half the width. PACKAGING: 310 ml cartridges, 550 ml soft cartridges and 25 kg buckets.

profiles.label: Butt or expansion joint, rectangular section

mapei/mapeflex-ac4.caveat: This sheet prints no consumption table at all, only the width to depth rule above and the pack sizes, so the quantity here is computed from the joint volume, which is exact arithmetic, and is not a figure quoted from the sheet. The depths come from the sheet's own printed rule. Also available in 550 ml soft cartridges and 25 kg buckets. The sheet caps joint movement at 12.5 percent of the width and asks for a primer coat for a heavy duty seal.

mapei/mapeflex-pu-65.reason: The sheet publishes a density and nothing else: 1.2 kg per litre of components A and B. It prints no joint table and no width to depth rule, so there is no sheet figure to size a joint from. The joint volume in litres, which is the width times the depth in millimetres times the length divided by 1000, times 1.2 gives the kilogrammes, and it is supplied in 10 kg drums of A plus B. It can be extended with Quartz 0.50 up to 1 to 1 by weight, which changes the quantity again.

mapei/mapeproof-swell.reason: The sheet gives one figure rather than a joint table: each 320 ml cartridge forms about 3 linear metres of a 6 to 13 mm diameter swelling bead, so order one cartridge per 3 metres, in boxes of 6. That is a bead laid on a surface, not a joint of a measured width and depth, so there is nothing to calculate from a section.

mapei/mapeflex-express-80-400.reason: CONSUMPTION: according to the volume of the hole to be filled. The sheet prints no rate per metre or per square metre, because this is a two component repair resin poured into cracks and holes. It is supplied in 600 ml bi-axial cartridges, boxes of 8 with static mixers, and in 20 litre buckets of each component.

vetonit/vetoflex-pu780.reason: No data sheet is hosted for Vetoflex PU780 yet, so there is no printed joint table and no width to depth schedule to size a joint from. The only published figure we hold is the pack, 600 ml sausages. Millilitres per linear metre are the joint width times the depth in millimetres, but the depth a joint needs is a property of the sealant and is not ours to assume from another brand, so no quantity is offered here until the sheet is in.

mapei/adesilex-mt-32.source: CONSUMPTION: coverage varies, depending on the evenness of the walls and the back of the wall covering. MAPEI No. 1 trowel from 200 to 250 g/m2, trowel TKB A1/A4 150 to 250 g/m2, roller approx. 200 g/m2, brush approx. 150 g/m2.

tiers.label: MAPEI No. 1 trowel
tiers.hint: The sheet's first named tool for wall coverings

mapei/adesilex-mt-32.caveat: The rows are tools, not sizes, and they are in the sheet's printed order, so the default is the sheet's own first row and also its highest rate rather than the cheapest. The sheet prints the figures in grammes per square metre: 200 to 250 g/m2 is 0.2 to 0.25 kg/m2. Also supplied in 10, 5 and 1 kg buckets. On dusty or absorbent substrates the sheet asks for a primer first, or a coat of Adesilex MT32 itself diluted 1 to 2 with water, which is extra.

mapei/mapecoat-tns-base-coat.source: CONSUMPTION (referred to undiluted product applied on a bituminous conglomerate substrate): porous substrates, first coat 0.4 to 0.6 kg/m2 and second coat 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2; non porous substrates, first coat 0.2 to 0.4 kg/m2 and second coat 0.1 to 0.3 kg/m2.

tiers.label: Porous substrate, first and second coat
tiers.hint: 0.4 to 0.6 plus 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 as printed

tiers.label: Non porous substrate, first and second coat
tiers.hint: 0.2 to 0.4 plus 0.1 to 0.3 kg/m2 as printed

mapei/mapecoat-tns-base-coat.caveat: Each row is the sheet's two printed coats added together, which is how the system is actually laid; the sheet prints the coats separately as 0.4 to 0.6 then 0.3 to 0.5 on a porous substrate and 0.2 to 0.4 then 0.1 to 0.3 on a non porous one. The figures are for undiluted product on a bituminous conglomerate, and the sheet has the binder mixed with 0.1 to 0.5 mm quartz sand and diluted with water before use, which the figures do not include. The default is the porous row because it is the heavier of the two.

mapei/mapecoat-tns-binder.source: CONSUMPTION: approximately 0.9 to 1.2 kg/m2 for application on even substrates with a rubber trowel, referring to concentrated product applied as indicated in the Preparation of the product section.

tiers.label: Even substrate, rubber trowel
tiers.hint: Concentrated product, as prepared on the sheet

mapei/mapecoat-tns-binder.caveat: The sheet opens the same paragraph with a warning that consumption of the first coats is heavily influenced by the absorption and roughness of the substrate, so on a rough or thirsty court the first coat will take more than this.

mapei/mapefloor-cleaner-ed.reason: This is a concentrated detergent for washing a finished resin floor, not a coating, so the sheet publishes a dilution rather than a coverage: use it at 1 to 3 percent, which is 100 to 300 g in 10 litres of water, and increase the concentration on porous or heavily soiled surfaces. It is supplied in 10 kg cans. How far a can goes depends on how much wash water the floor takes, which the sheet does not state.

mapei/mapefloor-decor-700.source: CONSUMPTION: from 1 to 1.5 kg/m2 per layer, depending on the characteristics of the substrate and the type of decorative effect desired.

pack.label: unit of components A and B

layers.name: Repair of cracks, holes and irregularities with Eporip, Mapefloor EP19, Mapefloor JA or Mapefloor JA Fast, where the substrate needs it
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: Primer SN mixed with about 20 percent by weight of Quartz 0.5, lightly broadcast with Quartz 0.5 while wet
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: First layer, Mapefloor Decor 700 with about 7 percent Mapecolor Paste, diluted with 2 to 20 percent water, then sanded
Second layer, Mapefloor Decor 700, diluted with no more than 10 percent water
Finishing layer, at least two coats of a transparent polyurethane finish from the Mapefloor Finish range
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

layers.name: Optional wax, Mapelux Opaca or Mapelux Lucida over the whole floor
layers.rate: no rate printed on this sheet

mapei/mapefloor-decor-700.caveat: The sheet's system is two layers of Mapefloor Decor 700, so 2 to 3 kg/m2 of this product, for a finished thickness of 1.5 to 3 mm. Supplied in 10 kg units, component A 2 kg plus component B 8 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-ep-19-me.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor EP19 ME 22 kg/m2 per cm of thickness. Primer SN 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the absorption of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A, B and C

mapei/mapefloor-ep-19-me.caveat: 22 kg/m2 per cm is 2.2 kg/m2 per mm, and the default of 10 mm is the sheet's own centimetre. The sheet prints no thickness range for the screed, so the 5 to 30 mm bounds on the control are a practical range and not a sheet figure. Primer SN is a separate line at 0.3 to 0.5 kg/m2 and is not in this quantity; it comes in 20 kg kits. The kit is 1.6 kg of A plus 0.8 kg of B plus 24 kg of C and must be mixed whole.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-415-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.3 to 0.8 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-415-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The range also moves with the particle size of the broadcast quartz sand under the finish. The kit is 10 kg of A plus 2.5 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-450-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.2 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit (18.90 kg of A plus 3.60 kg of B)

mapei/mapefloor-finish-450-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The sheet lists the two components separately, 18.90 kg of A and 3.60 kg of B, rather than naming a kit weight.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-451.reason: The sheet prints a theoretical consumption of 0.2 to 0.8 kg/m2 and says in the same breath that it depends on the roughness of the substrate and that higher temperatures increase it. A four to one range is not a figure to multiply an area by, so the sheet's own range is shown instead of a calculated quantity. It is supplied as 14 kg of component A plus 6 kg of component B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-460-me.source: CONSUMPTION: theoretical consumption 0.2 to 0.5 kg/m2 depending on the selected system.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-460-me.caveat: Consumption depends on the roughness of the substrate, the surrounding temperature and the type of tool used. The figures are theoretical and are for a substrate between +15 and +35 degrees C; lower temperatures increase both the consumption and the hardening time. The sheet recommends preliminary tests to establish the real rate. The kit is 14 kg of A plus 6 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-52-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 50 to 150 g/m2 per coat, depending on the characteristics of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-52-w.caveat: The sheet prints 50 to 150 g/m2, which is 0.05 to 0.15 kg/m2, and the figure is per coat. It gives a waiting time between coats of 6 to 24 hours, so two coats is the normal build and the default here. The kit is 4.7 kg of A plus 0.7 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-53-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the characteristics of the substrate.
mapei/mapefloor-finish-53-w.caveat: No pack figure is offered because the sheet quotes the rate in kilogrammes but the pack in litres: a 5.5 litre kit, 5.0 litres of component A plus 0.5 litres of B. Converting between the two would need a density the sheet does not print. The sheet describes applying a second coat, with sanding if the maximum waiting time is exceeded, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-58-w.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.1 to 0.2 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the roughness and porosity of the substrate.

pack.label: kit of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-58-w.caveat: The rate is per coat and the sheet applies the finish in one or two coats, so two is the default here. On cementitious surfaces the sheet requires a primer first, which is a separate product. The kit is 5 kg of A plus 0.5 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-finish-htr.source: CONSUMPTION: 0.050 to 0.150 kg/m2 per coat, depending on the type of substrate to be covered.

pack.label: can of components A and B

mapei/mapefloor-finish-htr.caveat: The rate is per coat and the sheet applies it evenly in one or two coats by short pile roller or airless spray, so two is the default here. The can is 7 kg of A plus 3 kg of B.

mapei/mapefloor-i-500-w.source: CONSUMPTION, 1. Multi-layer slip-resistant system, thickness approx. 3 mm (Mapefloor System 51): primer Mapecoat I 600 W 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m2, light broadcast with Quartz 0.5 at 0.5 kg/m2, base layer Mapefloor I 500 W at 2.5 kg/m2, broadcast in excess with Quartz 0.5 at 5 kg/m2, finishing layer Mapefloor I 500 W at 0.7 kg/m2.

pack.label: unit (2 kg of A plus 24 kg of B)

layers.name: Primer, Mapecoat I 600 W (A plus B), if required
Base layer, Mapefloor I 500 W (A plus B plus Mapecolor Paste)
Finishing layer, Mapefloor I 500 W (A plus B plus Mapecolor Paste)

mapei/mapefloor-i-500-w.caveat: This is System 51, the 3 mm slip resistant build up, and the two Mapefloor I 500 W layers in it come to 3.2 kg/m2 of this product. The sheet prints two other build ups: System 52 at about 5 mm adds an intermediate layer of 2.5 kg/m2 with another 5 kg/m2 broadcast, so 5.7 kg/m2 of this product; and System 53, a smooth self levelling floor 2 to 4 mm thick, is 2 kg/m2 per mm of thickness, so 4 kg/m2 at 2 mm. The 0.15 to 0.50 kg/m2 line is the primer, a different product, and is not this floor's rate. All the rates are theoretical, assume Quartz 0.5 for the broadcast, and move with the condition, absorbency, roughness and temperature of the surface.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-cove.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/COVE approx. 2 kg per litre, depending on the shape and volume of the detail. For covings the typical consumptions are 0.9 kg/m for 3 cm x 3 cm, 1.6 kg/m for 4 cm x 4 cm and 2.5 kg/m for 5 cm x 5 cm.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-cove.caveat: A coving is a triangular fillet, so the volume per metre is half the product of its two legs in millimetres: a 3 by 3 cm coving is 450 ml per metre, 4 by 4 cm is 800 ml and 5 by 5 cm is 1250 ml. At the sheet's printed 2 kg per litre those are 0.9, 1.6 and 2.5 kg per metre, which is exactly what the sheet prints, 3 of 3 cells. Divide the millilitres by 1000 and multiply by 2 for kilogrammes. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 25 kg and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-mf.source: CONSUMPTION: as scratch coat at 1 mm thickness approx. 1.7 kg/m2; as self-smoothing layer, 3 mm approx. 5.5 kg/m2, 4 mm approx. 7 kg/m2, 6 mm approx. 10 kg/m2.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-mf.caveat: Only the sheet's own four printed rows are offered and nothing in between, because the table is not linear and disagrees with the sheet's own 1.7 kg/m2 per mm: 5.5 over 3 mm is 1.83 per mm and 10 over 6 mm is 1.67, an eight percent spread, so interpolating would be our arithmetic rather than Mapei's. Consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate and by site conditions. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 20 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg, and one batch is two packs of A, two of B, one sack of C and two of Mapecolor.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-rt.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/RT approx. 2.0 kg/m2 per mm thickness. 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-rt.caveat: The printed rate is linear and reproduces every printed row exactly: 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2. The control is bounded by the thicknesses the sheet prints. Consumption is influenced by the roughness and absorption of the substrate and by site conditions. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 18.5 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-ud.source: CONSUMPTION: Mapefloor CPU+/UD approx. 2.0 kg/m2 per mm thickness. 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2, 12 mm thickness approx. 24 kg/m2.
mapei/mapefloor-cpu-ud.caveat: The printed rate is linear and reproduces every printed row exactly: 6 mm thickness approx. 12 kg/m2, 9 mm thickness approx. 18 kg/m2, 12 mm thickness approx. 24 kg/m2. mapei/mapefloor-cpu-tc.source: CONSUMPTION: as topcoat on concrete or on a Mapefloor CPU+ product, Mapefloor CPU+/TC 0.4 to 1.2 kg/m2 depending on the roughness of the substrate.

tiers.label: Topcoat on concrete or on a Mapefloor CPU+ floor
tiers.hint: The range is the roughness of the substrate

mapei/mapefloor-cpu-tc.caveat: A three to one range, so treat the high end as the figure for a rough or open substrate. No pack is offered because the product is mixed from several packs: component A 2 kg, component B 2.16 kg, component C 2.5 kg bag and Mapecolor CPU+ 0.23 kg.

mapei/mapelux-lucida.caveat: The sheet prints a single figure, 50 g/m2, which is 0.05 kg/m2, and it is per coat: Mapelux Lucida is spread as a first coat and then, once that has dried, a second coat at right angles to it, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/mapelux-opaca.caveat: The sheet prints a single figure, 50 g/m2, which is 0.05 kg/m2, and it is per coat: Mapelux Opaca is spread as a first coat and then, once that has dried, a second coat at right angles to it, so two coats is the default here.

mapei/topcem.source: CONSUMPTION: consumption varies in relation to the thickness of the screed and the dosage of Topcem. For doses of 200 to 250 kg of Topcem per m3 of aggregates, consumption is 2 to 2.5 kg/m2/cm of thickness.
mapei/topcem.caveat: This is the binder only, not the finished screed. 2 to 2.5 kg/m2 per cm is 0.2 to 0.25 kg/m2 per mm, and it holds only at the sheet's dosage of 200 to 250 kg of Topcem per cubic metre of aggregate; the sand is a separate order, silt free and graded 0 to 6 mm. The sheet's own build ups are bonded screeds 10 to 40 mm thick, unbonded screeds at least 40 mm and floating screeds at least 55 mm, all to BS 8204-1:2003, which is where the 10 to 80 mm bounds and the 40 mm default come from.

mapei/topcem-pronto.source: CONSUMPTION: the consumption of Topcem Pronto is about 18 to 20 kg/m2 per cm thickness depending on the compaction degree.
mapei/topcem-pronto.caveat: 18 to 20 kg/m2 per cm is 1.8 to 2.0 kg/m2 per mm, and where in that range a job lands depends on how hard the screed is compacted. This is a ready mixed screed, so unlike Topcem no aggregate is added. The sheet's printed build ups run from 10 to 80 mm, bonded 30 to 80 mm, unbonded 35 to 80 mm, with at least 3 cm over the pipes of a heated screed.

kerakoll/quarzo.caveat: This is the one accessory with a published rate per square metre, and it covers only the broadcast for tacking. mapei/mapetex-sel.source: PACKAGING: Mapetex Sel is available in 25 m long rolls with a width of 1 m. APPLICATION: adjacent sheets of Mapetex Sel must overlap by at least 5 cm at both the longitudinal and transverse junction points.
